newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Selling of several blue chips led by tobacco heavyweight Sampoerna dragged down Jakarta share prices on Monday, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed 5.27 points, or 0.75 percent, lower at 700.11 points after touching an intra-day low of 698.14 points. Losers led gainers by 76 to 52, with 60 counters unchanged. Total turnover was 457.1 billion rupiah on a volume of 183.4 million shares.
"Possible continued selling of Sampoerna and other blue-chips might push down overall market sentiment on Tuesday," a local broker said.
But the index was likely to remain around 700 points on Tuesday with likely fresh buying in some medium and small-sized stocks, other brokers said.

"This is a period when the market is testing the level above 700 points. Some players were adopting a wait-and-see attitude. It was shown by a relatively small volume today," another local broker said.
Brokers said the sell-off of Sampoerna and Indofood pushed down market sentiment and prompted profit-taking in several blue-chips such as Telkom, Citra Marga and Bank Negara Indonesia.
Further selling in Sampoerna was prompted by news that it sees overseas subsidiary Sampoerna International making losses for the next three or four years, brokers said.
"That report led to further downside on Sampoerna, which was already weak following its lower-than-expected 1996 results," a foreign broker said.
Sampoerna finished down 2.52 percent at 11,600 rupiah on a volume of about two million shares. The stock has tumbled about 19.2 percent from Wednesday's closing price of 14,350 rupiah.
Noodle maker Indofood, part of the Salim group, fell 125 rupiah to 5,225 rupiah on a volume of 570,000 shares.
Brokers said the loss was due to the implications of a proposed rights issue to acquire some companies within the group, which has led to mixed reactions among analysts.
Property firm Elang Realty was the most active stock with about 26 million shares traded, but fell 50 rupiah to 925 rupiah due to profit-taking, brokers said.
They said some investors liquidated recent profits after news that privately-owned Bakrie Group acquired 70 percent of the company.
Shares of secondary hotel and property owner PT Sahid Jaya were also active due to market speculation of a possible rights issue, brokers said.
But the company's corporate secretary told Reuters that it was considering a rights issue among other action to finance its expansion programme, but nothing had been finalised yet.
Sahid Jaya rose 500 rupiah, or 35.71 percent, to close at 1,900 rupiah with about 12 million shares traded.
